chunks: The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) informed us from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh from his father from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Isma'il ibn Marar and Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Mubarik from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who was obligated to fast two consecutive months, so he fasted twenty-five days, then he became ill. When he recovered, should he build upon what he had fasted, or should he repeat the entire fast? He said: Rather, he builds upon what he had fasted. Then he said: This is what Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has made easy for him, and there is no penalty upon him for what Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has made easy for him.

key_terms.غَلَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: What Allah has made easy / facilitated

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for expiatory fasting if one gets sick and breaks the consecutive days?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for expiatory fasting (kaffarat), illness constitutes a valid excuse where the days already completed are counted, and the remaining days are made up after recovery, rather than restarting the entire period. This ruling is grounded in the principle of *al-ghalabah* (dominance of hardship), where the divine ease provided for the sick prevents the penalty of restarting. This specific fiqh nuance highlights the Shia emphasis on proportionality in acts of worship when interrupted by unavoidable circumstances.
